source.snippet: Ask HN: 'I'm curious if anyone here still actually writes code, in any meaningful amount, because they actually still need to. Excluding reasons like fun / learning. I loved coding in the past, but no matter what I do at this point, I can't find a reason to anymore that's actually necessary.' 6 points, 9 comments.

problem_statement: Experienced software developers find their coding skills becoming redundant as AI handles implementation, leaving them without a clear professional identity or a structured path to higher-value roles that leverage their technical background.
target_segment: Mid-to-senior software engineers at tech companies and agencies facing AI-driven role displacement who need career repositioning support.
notes: Buyer signal is moderate — the poster is employed (implied), technically experienced, and the 9-comment thread suggests resonance. Opportunity: a paid coaching or structured curriculum service helping senior devs pivot to AI-adjacent roles (prompt engineering lead, AI product manager, technical architect). Willingness to pay not explicit but career-transition services command $500–$5k+ per customer. De-prioritized slightly vs. stronger buyer signals.
